newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields continue to rally in election's wake.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields continue to rally in election's wake.

text.p: New Zealand yields continued to drop away at Monday's close, rallying nearly 30 basis points in the first trading session after an election which left the country without a clear idea of the make-up of its next government.

The benchmark 10-year and three-year bonds rallied 27 basis points over the day, to 7.79 percent and 7.78 percent respectively. In the money market, 90-day bank bill rates were down eight at 9.84 percent. Dealers said bills had seen much of their rally on Friday in a burst of short-covering and were comfortable around current levels.

After Saturday's general election, neither the ruling conservative National party or the main opposition Labour party can form a majority coalition without the support of the New Zealand First Party. NZ First has yet to say which way it will lean, and coalition talks are expected to take weeks.
The result was very much in line with pre-election polling and carried few surprises. Dealers noted ratings agency Standard and Poor's said it was broadly comfortable with the outcome.
They said some players had been caught short by the lack of adverse market reaction to the election, and were scrambling to cover positions.
One dealer said some also seemed to be holding out hopes that National and New Zealand First could reach a deal.
"We're probably clutching at straws, but if the market wants to rally they'll try to find any information they can."
Another dealer said the session had seen a number of offshore buying flows from players more concerned with chasing high yields than with political uncertainty.
He expected the market to open on Tuesday around current levels, saying it could not sustain its current pace but was also unlikely to retrace.

Tuesday's Consumer Price Index and underlying inflation data were not expected to stray far from the market's pick of a 0.6 percent rise in underlying inflation in the September quarter, for a 2.6 percent annual rise.

"Certainly it may do the short end some harm if the CPI comes in high. It could put a bit of pressure on there, but I suspect the market wants to buy it anyway so I can't see too much weakness," one dealer said.
NZD VS 3 YR 10 YR * NZD 3-YR/10-YR SPREAD

New Zealand bonds outperformed other dollar bloc countries on the back of short-covering on Monday, the first trading session after Saturday's inconclusive general election. The NZ/US 10-year spread narrowed to 127 points over, from nearly 150 points reached in thin pre-election trade on Friday.
